item.title: Canadian publisher with 25 million Facebook followers loses Meta claim over 2020 shutdown
item.description: A Canadian online publisher suffered significant losses when Meta permanently removed its Facebook pages in 2020. The publisher, which had millions of followers, argued that this removal violated its business rights. Despite submitting numerous advertisements, many faced rejection for policy violations, which included misleading content. A court upheld Meta's decision, emphasizing its protection under Section 230 of the Communications Decency Act. Fuente: The Times of India - World.

item.title: How the Zhuhai air show charted China’s path from catching up to flying high
item.description: When Zhuhai hosted its inaugural air show in November 1996, the event showcased the J-8IIM fighter, a second-generation fighter equipped with Russian radar and weapons, alongside a limited line-up of home-made aircraft. Imported planes were the focus and Chinese audiences curiously studied the much more advanced foreign designs. They crowded around two Russian fourth-generation Su-27 fighters and were wowed as the jets performed their famous cobra manoeuvre, sharply braking in mid-air. At the...
